newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-JORDAN BECOMES FIRST WITH TWO MILLION ALL-STAR VOTES.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-JORDAN BECOMES FIRST WITH TWO MILLION ALL-STAR VOTES.

text.p: Chicago Bulls guard Michael Jordan became the first player to receive more than two million votes in one season when final returns of fan balloting for the 1997 NBA All-Star Game were released Sunday.
The 46th annual NBA All-Star Game will be played at Gund Arena in Cleveland on February 9.
Jordan led all NBA vote-getters for the eighth time in his career with 2,451,136, and is the all-time leader in votes received with over 12 million.

He will be joined in the Eastern Conference starting lineup by Orlando Magic guard Penny Hardaway, Detroit Pistons forward Grant Hill, Bulls forward Scottie Pippen and New York Knicks centre Patrick Ewing.
Forwards Charles Barkley of the Houston Rockets and Shawn Kemp of the Seattle SuperSonics were the top vote-getters in the Western Conference.
Joining Barkley and Kemp, who will start together for the third straight year, are Houston centre Hakeem Olajuwon, Seattle guard Gary Payton and Utah Jazz guard John Stockton.

Barkley was the top vote-getter in the West with 1,877,232 and was followed closely by Kemp's 1,713,049. Karl Malone of Utah finished third at forward with 1,337,319, while the Minnesota Timberwolves' Kevin Garnett had 481,911.
Olajuwon compiled 1,487,310 votes, just ahead of Shaquille O'Neal of the Los Angeles Lakers, who had 1,305,941. San Antonio Spurs big man David Robinson, who is hurt, placed third with 753,247.
Payton collected 1,206,539 votes, while Stockton came in with 1,127,250. Houston's Clyde Drexler finished a respectable third with 926,431 and the Phoenix Suns' Jason Kidd had 911,858.
It was the 12th All-Star selection for Olajuwon, the 11th for Barkley, ninth for Stockton, fifth for Kemp and fourth for Payton.
Hill, who led all players in votes received in 1995 and 1996, collected 1,868,020 votes this year and was followed at forward by Pippen's 1,683,596.

Chicago's Dennis Rodman, who is suspended at least through the All-Star Game for kicking a cameraman, finished third with 887,483, while Washington Bullets front-court mates Chris Webber and Juwon Howard were fourth and fifth, respectively.

Hardaway, who has been limited to just 15 games due to injury, finished with 1,132,024 votes. Philadelphia 76ers rookie Allen Iverson placed third at guard with 567,641 and Reggie Miller of the Indiana Pacers jumped to fourth with 506,553.

Ewing bested fellow Georgetown product Alonzo Mourning of the Miami Heat, 1,395,759 to 1,041,570, for the starting job. Dikembe Mutombo of the Atlanta Hawks -- also of Georgetown -- claimed third place at 541,528.
It was the 11th All-Star selection for Jordan and Ewing, the seventh for Pippen and the third for both Hill and Hardaway.
All NBA head coaches will vote for the remaining members of the All-Star teams in their respective conferences, and their selections will be announced on Tuesday or Wednesday.
